en: The Therāpadāna, Metteyyavagga: 1.
The Apadāna of the Elder Tissa-Metteyya
“Relying on Pabbhārakūṭa,
an ascetic named Sobhita lived there,
subsisting on wild fruits that had fallen of their own accord.”
He was dwelling in the midst of the mountains.
At that time, having brought wood, I kindled a fire.
Seeking the supreme goal for rebirth in the Brahma-world,
Padumuttara, the Knower of the World, [arose].
He is the receiver of offerings;
desiring to uplift me,
he has come into my presence.
“What are you doing, O one of great merit?
Give me firewood for the fire;
I shall attend to the fire.”
"Then my purification will come to pass.
"You are Subhaddaka among men,
O deity, you understand this."
“Attend to the fire;
here, take wood for your fire.
Then, having taken the wood,
The Conqueror kindled a fire;
there no wood was burned—
such was the miracle of the Great Seer.
“Your fire does not blaze,
your oblation does not exist;
indeed, your ascetic practice is useless.”
“Worship the fire for me.
“Of what kind, O Great Hero,
is that fire spoken of by you?”
“Let this be told to me as well;
let us both attend upon you.
“For the sake of the cessation of the phenomena of cause—”
And for the subduing of the defilements—
having abandoned envy and avarice,
these three are my offerings.”
‘Of what sort are you, O Great Hero?
What is your lineage, dear sir?
What is your conduct and practice?’
"I truly find this deeply pleasing:
born into a kshatriya family,
you have reached the perfection of direct knowledge."
"All taints are utterly destroyed;
there is now no further becoming.
"If you are a Buddha, all-knowing,"
Light-maker, dispeller of darkness;
I shall pay homage to you, O Lord,
for you are the ender of suffering.”
Having spread out a deer-skin,
I offered it as a seat;
sit down, O Lord, All-Knowing One.
"I shall attend upon you.
There the Blessed One sat down upon a well-spread antelope skin.
Having invited the Fully Awakened One,
I went to the mountain,
having filled a khārī-measure of provisions.
I brought a tinduka fruit;
having mixed it with honey,
I gave that fruit to the Buddha.
While I was reflecting on this,
the Jina then partook [of it];
there I gained confidence in my mind.
Beholding the Leader of the World—
Padumuttara, the Knower of the Worlds,
the recipient of offerings.
Having sat down in the assembly hall,
he spoke these verses:
“He who satisfied me with fruit— ”
With serene and wholesome hands,
I shall extol him;
listen as I speak.
Twenty-five times he will exercise sovereignty over the gods;
and a thousand times he will be a king.
"He will become a wheel-turning monarch.
Perceiving his intention,
[the deity] took account of his past karma.
Food, drink, clothing,
and costly bedding—
these are joined with meritorious deeds.
They shall be reborn at that very time;
and he too shall always be joyful and free from ailment.
Whatever womb one is reborn into—
whether as a deity or as a human—
one becomes happy in every state.
He will attain human birth as one who recites the scriptures,
a bearer of the mantras,
and one who has mastered the three Vedas.

Having approached the Perfectly Enlightened One, he will become an Arahant. As far as I can remember myself, I have never seen such a thing before. Even when the Teacher was staying at Sāvatthī, I did not see him with my own eyes. But now that I have seen him, I shall surely attain the fruit of stream-entry. “Venerable sir, what was the name of the Blessed One at that time? “He was named Saradaññā Tathāgata, Arhat, Perfectly Enlightened One. “But, venerable sir, how long ago was that? “That was one hundred thousand aeons ago. “Venerable sir, it has been a long time since I attained the fruit of stream-entry. It was on that very day, venerable sir, that I attained the fruit of stream-entry. “It is wonderful, Venerable Anuruddha, it is marvelous, Venerable Anuruddha, how well this was said by you: ‘Venerable sir, it has been a long time since I attained the fruit of stream-entry. It was on that very day, venerable sir, that I attained the fruit of stream-entry. “Venerable sir, it is not surprising that I attained the fruit of stream-entry on that very day. For the Blessed One, the Arahant, the Perfectly Enlightened One, spoke these words to me: ‘Anuruddha, do you wish to go to the Himālaya mountains? ‘I do, Blessed One,’ I replied. ‘Then, Anuruddha, take five hundred monks and go to the Himālaya mountains. There you will find a delightful spot—cool, pleasant, with a clear stream flowing along a rocky bed, remote from the crowd, suitable for retreat. Build a dwelling there and live in seclusion. When you have lived there for seven years, you will become an Arahant. Since I can remember myself, venerable sir, I have never heard these words spoken by anyone else. But when I heard them spoken by the Blessed One, I attained the fruit of stream-entry. “It is wonderful, Venerable Anuruddha, it is marvelous, Venerable Anuruddha, how well this was said by you: ‘Venerable sir, it is not surprising that I attained the fruit of stream-entry on that very day. Since I have attained full maturity,
there is no deficiency in my wealth;
this is the fruit of giving fruit.
Having attained the supreme Dhamma,
he has utterly eradicated passion and hatred;
with all taints completely destroyed, he stands.
Now there is no further becoming.
My defilements are burnt away;
all states of existence have been uprooted.
Like a snake that has severed its bonds,
I dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to me!
In the presence of my Buddha,
the three knowledges have been attained;
the teaching of the Buddha has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges,
these eight liberations,
and the six supernormal powers have been realized.
“Thus was the teaching of the Buddha spoken.
In this way, it is said, the elder Venerable Tissa-Metteyya spoke these verses.
This is the first legend of the elder Tissa-Metteyya.
